description.narrative:
The project expands access to finance for MSMEs in Peru, with a strong focus on WMSMEs. IFCs loan enables Compartamos to increase short-term working capital lending, earmarking 75% of proceeds for women, building on an existing portfolio where women lead 64% by volume and 76% by client count. This targets a critical gap: only about 28% of MSMEs use the regulated financial system and informal financing needs are large. Women entrepreneurs face collateral, informality, and access barriers yet exhibit lower delinquency, making them an attractive and underserved segment. The project aims to narrow gender gaps in account ownership and credit access while addressing working capital constraints for informal and low-income entrepreneurs. IFC will track the number and volume of outstanding loans to MSEs and WMSEs and the MSME share of the banks portfolio.
At the market level, the project fosters financial inclusion by demonstrating the commercial viability of group lending for low-income microentrepreneurs. Compartamos, Perus leading and first scaled provider of this model, operates a tech-enabled approach with weekly repayments, pre-credit training, group incentives, and specialized loan officers, yielding better repayment performance in group loans than in individual loans. By evidencing lower risk and efficiency at scale, the project is expected to catalyze replication by other microfinance institutions, extending reach to unserved borrowers.

The proposed investment comprises a senior unsecured loan of up to US$50 million equivalent in PEN to Compartamos Banco S.A. (Compartamos or the Bank), a subsidiary of Gentera S.A.B. de C.V. (Gentera), for IFCs own account with a tenor of five years, including a one-year principal grace period. The loan proceeds will be used to increase access to finance for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSME) and women-owned micro, small and medium enterprises (WSMEs) in Peru (the Project).

name.narrative: Compartamos is headquartered in Lima, Peru, and operates nationwide, serving over 1.2 million clients across 22 regions of the country. The Bank has 124 branches, more than 28,000 contact points, and over 6,360 employees, attending to clients in both urban and rural areas.
